Frequently Asked Questions What are the federal contract vehicles and procurement systems used? Contract vehicles are structured to allow agencies to purchase goods or services without starting a new competitive bidding process from scratch for every order. The most common vehicles include: GSA Multiple Award Schedules (MAS): Long-term contracts providing agencies access to commercial products and services at volume pricing. Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs): IT-specific contracts allowing multiple agencies to buy technology and services. Notable examples include Alliant, NASA SEWP, 8(a) STARS III, and CIO-SP. Multi-Agency Contracts (MACs): Similar to GWACs but covering complex professional services, such as OASIS and HCaTS. Agency-Specific IDIQs: Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity contracts created for a single agency's specific needs, like the Navy's SeaPort-NxG. Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs): Simplified methods for filling repetitive needs by establishing charge accounts with trusted vendors. To manage these purchases, the government uses several official digital procurement systems: SAM.gov: The primary official system to register your business and search for open contract opportunities. GSA Advantage!: An online shopping system for federal agencies to purchase directly from GSA Schedule contractors. GSA eBuy: An electronic Request for Quote (RFQ) system for agencies to request bids from GSA Schedule and GWAC holders. Contract vehicles are structured to allow agencies to purchase goods or services without starting a new competitive bidding process from scratch for every order. The most common vehicles include: GSA Multiple Award Schedules (MAS): Long-term contracts providing agencies access to commercial products and services at volume pricing. Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs): IT-specific contracts allowing multiple agencies to buy technology and services. Agency-Specific IDIQs: Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity contracts created for a single agency's specific needs, like the Navy's SeaPort-NxG. Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs): Simplified methods for filling repetitive needs by establishing charge accounts with trusted vendors. GSA Advantage!: An online shopping system for federal agencies to purchase directly from GSA Schedule contractors. Contract vehicles are structured to allow agencies to purchase goods or services without starting a new competitive bidding process from scratch for every order. The most common vehicles include: GSA Multiple Award Schedules (MAS): Long-term contracts providing agencies access to commercial products and services at volume pricing. Agency-Specific IDIQs: Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity contracts created for a single agency's specific needs, like the Navy's SeaPort-NxG. Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs): Simplified methods for filling repetitive needs by establishing charge accounts with trusted vendors.
